scope: Local authored tiny C experiment; no Chromium source or engine compilation

cases.scope: Local tiny authored C interrupt/state-flush experiment; no engine source
Local tiny authored C experiment after completed-step acknowledgement; not engine acceptance

fixture_sources.main.c: int answer(void); int main(void) { return answer(); }
fixture_sources.build.ninja:
rule cc
  command = /usr/bin/cc -MMD -MF $out.d -c $in -o $out
  depfile = $out.d
  deps = gcc
rule link
  command = /usr/bin/sleep 8 && /usr/bin/cc $in -o $out
build a.o: cc a.c
build main.o: cc main.c
build sample: link a.o main.o
default sample

method: Launch Siso in a new process group, signal only that owned group with SIGINT, wait for exit/state flush, copy its owned workspace/state preserving file metadata back to the same absolute path, then invoke Siso and execute the produced sample. The first case signalled when object files appeared; the second waited for two native completion acknowledgements and link start.
conclusion: File existence did not prove a completed native step: the first case acknowledged zero steps and safely rebuilt all three. After two acknowledged steps, the interrupted state reused both objects and executed only one final link; the program returned7.
limitations: Same local Linux machine and exact workspace path; not a two-runner result.
SIGINT is not evidence that SIGKILL or process-tree termination flushes valid state.
Does not prove Chromium intermediate size/provenance, Windows SDK/state resumption, cache allowance or final engine link fit.
